main_text.p: nua concussuræ in pedes erectæ consistere.
2.[?] Torris seu Ἀχλὸς[?], ubi exhalatio bene compacta una tantum parte accenditur.
4. Stellæ discurrentes, ubi exhalatio longius diductá in multas easdemq; exiguas particulas disseminata existit, & latitudo & crassitudo consimiliter se habent.

Ex his facile potest de alijs eiusdem generis, ut de igne perpendiculari, lancea ardente, igne fatuo, igne lambente, Dracone uolante, similibusq;, quæ non ab Aristotele, sed ab alijs scriptoribus nominantur, iudicari.
In perpendiculo, exhalationis portio crassior in imo subsidet, subtilior sursum vergit in mucronem.
In lancea ardente, uel iaculo, exhalatio per omnia subtilis est, & in rectum diductá: sed alicubi paulo densior, alicubi rarior.
In igne fatuo, siue Castore ac Polluce, exhalatio crassa est & pinguis, quæ leui flatu huc illucq; protruditur, & propter crassitiem sæpe visitur in locis humilioribus.
Ignis lambens ad iubas equorum, ad vestes hominum exilit, quasi lambendo eas. producitur ex tenuibus exhalationibus, plerunque è sudoribus deductis.

page.notes: The Greek word after "Torris seu" is printed in a form that appears to contain a Latin-looking x; the reading Ἀχλὸς is uncertain. The number before "Torris" is printed as a character resembling "ȝ" and is read as 2. The line "calida, al-" is continued on the next page. The printed "uergit" was normalised to "vergit" and "uel" and "uolans" are kept as printed in spelling.
